title: Cooking with fire without burning down the kitchen: Dominik Kundel
talk_summary: Dominik Kundel describes Twilio's 16-person Emerging Tech & Innovation team, which prototypes AI products fast, ships rough versions under an 'alpha' sub-brand to set expectations, and treats every model as replaceable.

takeaways.what_they_do: They assume any model they use will be redundant soon, so they keep a list of known limitations and a fast way to validate whether a newly released model helps, deciding within a day whether to adopt or backlog it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we assume that every model that we're using is going to be redundant tomorrow ... how do we quickly validate whether the next model is something that helps us
takeaways.numbers: decided within a day whether to pay attention to a new model (3.5 Sonic)

takeaways.technique: Alpha sub-brand to ship rough work early
takeaways.what_they_do: They created a separate 'Twilio Alpha' brand to set lower reliability expectations, letting them ship rough prototypes to real users early and often without violating the main product's quality bar.
takeaways.evidence_quote: create our own sub brand cult fio Alpha that was very focused on um you know setting the right expectations with customers but enabling us therefore to ship early

takeaways.technique: Dogfooding on a low-risk internal use case
takeaways.what_they_do: Before targeting real customers, they deployed their agent builder on an internal help-desk use case to gather data and surface quality problems in a low-risk setting.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we started with a low uh lowrisk use case around it help desk ... it was a way for us to gather data and see what the quality challenges were

takeaways.what_they_do: Operating in isolation caused other teams to not know they existed and to duplicate or conflict; they now proactively share learnings internally and externally.
takeaways.evidence_quote: teams not even knowing that we existed as a team or what we were working on and it was on us to find potential conflicts
